subject: Day 52: reach for a play-gym toy
bodyText:
Today's focus
Avi is 52 days old and starting to turn looking into reaching. Today is about giving his hands a target under a play gym while the 2-month visit prep continues in the background.

Action items
- Lay him under a play gym with one toy hung just within arm's reach so passive looking starts to become batting and swiping. HealthyChildren on movement: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx
- Pre-fill 24 hours of formula or pumped milk ahead of the visit week, since vaccine-day fussiness can disrupt the feeding rhythm.
- Verify infant acetaminophen is in the cabinet and the weight-based dose is written down, to treat after the shots if needed. AAP on immunizations: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/immunizations/aap-policy-on-immunizations/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Hiccups during or after feeds and wet sneezing; both are normal and self-limited.
- [monitor] Forceful arching during feeds with frequent painful spit-up or refusal despite hunger cues, which can point to reflux or cow's-milk-protein intolerance; raise it at the 2-month visit.
- [call within 24h] Lethargy that is out of proportion to recent activity, or a feeding refusal pattern that runs more than 24 hours.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C) under 90 days, cyanosis around the lips, or labored breathing means call now or dial 911!

Enrichment opportunities
- Hang or hold a toy just out of reach during tummy time and floor play so reaching motivates head lift and upper-body work. HealthyChildren on movement: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx
- Vary live-singing tempo across a session (slow lullaby, fast clapping song, then slow again) to preserve the rhythm and pitch range his brain is still tuning. Gerry et al. on infant music: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/
- Answer his increasingly varied coos with full back-and-forth turns, pausing for his reply; conversational turn-taking is the language-building unit. Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/

Upcoming
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit; vaccines HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, IPV #1.
- Day 57-72: post-vaccine 24-48h window of fussiness and low-grade fever.
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit; vaccines RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
